sections.html:
If speed matters, Janesville owners generally look at an agent, a sale on their own, or cash from a buyer who accepts the house untouched. About 66,929 people live in the city, a rise of 2.0 percent over the April 2020 base.

Putting the house on the market puts it in front of more buyers, but showings and a lender's timetable control your calendar. A cash deal shrinks the job to title review, a return and a recorded deed. The closing steps below fit both, and the vacant-building rule applies if the house stands empty.

Buyer demand rises and falls with local employment and the draw of nearby metro areas, so line your house up against recent Janesville sales rather than Madison or Chicago prices. Most people here own, with about two in three households in that group, and over 90 percent of residents did not move during the past year.

Owners of long standing often hold houses with few updates, and a buyer measuring yours against the $223,400 middle value will ask what has been replaced.

Interstate 90/39, U.S. 14 and 51, and state highways 26 and 11 all cross Janesville and lead toward Madison and Chicago. If your listing targets commuters, say so.

Average snowfall of 36.6 inches puts roofs, furnaces and basements under stress, and inspectors know it. Show buyers receipts for any recent work on them.

sections.h2: Vacant and rental rules in Janesville
sections.html:
The city makes owners register vacant properties. The ordinance sets these deadlines:

  • 90 days after a building becomes vacant;
  • 30 days after a transfer of ownership;
  • 30 days after a lender files a foreclosure summons and complaint in Rock County Circuit Court on residential property.

Absent an exemption in the city code, the first registration is $200 for a residential building and $350 for a commercial one, and the fee climbs every six months the property remains vacant. Owners must also keep inside and outside safe and sanitary. Questions go to (608) 755-3109.

Neighborhood and Community Services, reachable at (608) 755-3065, deals with nuisance debris, occupancy concerns, parking on residential lots and landlord-tenant matters. Complaints typically get an inspector within seven to ten days, and life-safety problems within a day or two. Open violations make an open-market sale harder, so ask about any notice before you list. Snow removal, tall grass and weeds go to the City Services Center instead.

sections.h2: Recording the deed in Rock County
sections.html:
Wisconsin charges the seller a transfer fee of 30 cents per $100 of value (Wis. Stat. 77.22). It is paid to the Rock County Register of Deeds when the deed is recorded, and the grantor and grantee each sign the electronic return. Papers can be handed in at the office or left in the lobby drop box at the courthouse.

A few deeds owe nothing. Under Wis. Stat. 77.25 the exempt group covers passage by will, descent or survivorship, parent-child transfers for nominal or no consideration, and foreclosure deeds to the mortgage holder. An heir preparing to sell a parent's house should ask the closing agent which line of the return fits.

Within ten days of accepting a contract, sellers of one-to-four unit homes must deliver a Real Estate Condition Report. When it is late, the buyer can rescind for two business days after the deadline (Wis. Stat. 709.02). Fiduciaries appointed by a court, including personal representatives, are excused when they never lived in the house.

The tax bill splits into two payments, January 31 and July 31. Money paid by January 31 goes to the local treasurer, and anything after that goes to the county (Wis. Stat. 74.11). The next date is January 31, 2027. Ask the City of Janesville treasurer for the exact balance before the title company prepares the settlement statement.

A Janesville sale follows a handful of steps in a set order, and laying them out makes each deadline easier to meet.

  • Write down the day you accept the contract, because it starts the 10-day clock for the condition report.
  • Deliver the report to the buyer, answering each question from what you know.
  • Check whether any city nuisance, occupancy or vacant-building item is open, and resolve or disclose it.
  • Have the electronic transfer return completed and signed by both sides.
  • File the deed at the Rock County Register of Deeds.
  • Pay off the mortgage and your share of taxes from the proceeds.

Cash purchasers skip appraisal and underwriting, which leaves your own paperwork as the pacing item. Borrowers add an inspection and loan approval. Your duties under state law stay the same in both cases, so build the move around whichever calendar applies.

sections.h2: Selling a rented or inherited house
sections.html:
A tenant normally keeps living there until the lease ends, so check the end date and notice terms before you promise a closing day. Buyers wanting a vacant house must reach terms with the tenant, and once empty the building falls under the vacant-building rule.

With an inherited house, first work out who may sign for the estate. If that person never lived there, the condition report is not required, and passage by will or descent owes no fee. A later sale is its own transfer, with the usual return and recording.

sections.h2: What to gather before you list
sections.html:
Keep a ready folder for when an offer arrives:

  • The most recent tax bill and any special assessment notices.
  • Records of repairs, replacements and permits for the roof, furnace and basement.
  • A note on whether any city nuisance or occupancy notice is open.
  • The payoff amount for any mortgage or lien.

Cash buyers look at much the same papers but ask fewer follow-up questions. If the house is rented, add the lease and the tenant's contact details. If it has sat empty, confirm that the vacant-building registration is current. If a payoff, assessment or permit question is still open, ask the office involved now. Waiting until a buyer's lender asks can add days to a closing that was meant to be quick.

faqs.q: Does Janesville require a vacant house to be registered?
faqs.a: Yes. Owners register within 90 days of a building going vacant, 30 days after ownership changes, or 30 days after a lender starts foreclosure on a residential property in Rock County Circuit Court. The first residential fee is $200 and rises every six months, with exemptions available in the city code.

faqs.q: What does the Janesville transfer fee come to?
faqs.a: Sellers pay 30 cents per $100 of value or fraction thereof, and the Rock County Register of Deeds collects it when the deed is recorded with the electronic return.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Janesville house that has code violations?
faqs.a: Call Neighborhood and Community Services at (608) 755-3065 to learn what remains open and what it takes to close it. Buyers will ask about open orders, so settle what you can first.

faqs.q: Who pays property tax after I sell in Janesville?
faqs.a: You and the buyer share the year's bill at closing, and the title company normally takes your portion from the proceeds. Because installments fall on January 31 and July 31, confirm the paid-to date with the treasurer.

faqs.q: Does an heir have to complete a condition report in Janesville?
faqs.a: Only if the heir has lived in the house. A personal representative, trustee or other court-supervised fiduciary who never did is excused, while an heir who lived there should deliver the report within 10 days of accepting a contract.
